problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}+8{x}^{2}+17x+8}{x(x+2)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+2}+\frac{C}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{D}{(x+2)^{3}},
$$

where $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are real constants, determine the value of $AB+CD.$

activity_context.topic_title: Expressing Rational Functions with Repeated Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-x+4}{(x+2)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x+2}+\frac{B}{(x+2)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+2)^{3}},
$$

where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are real constants, find the value of $A\cdot B+C.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+2)^{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-x+4 & =A(x+2)^{2}+B(x+2)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-2$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2)^{2}-(-2)+4 & =A(-2+2)^{2}+B(-2+2)+C \\ 10 & =A(0)+B(0)+C \\ C & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(0)^{2}-(0)+4 & =A(0+2)^{2}+B(0+2)+10 \\ 4 & =4A+2B+10 \\ 0 & =4A+2B+6 \\ 0 & =2A+B+3 \\ B & =-2A-3.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x=-1$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2}-(-1)+4 & =A(-1+2)^{2}+B(-1+2)+10 \\ 6 & =A+B+10 \\ 0 & =A+B+4 \\ B & =-4-A.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-2A-3 & =-4-A \\ -A & =-1 \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $A$ into $(2)$  to get the value of $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =-4-1=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B+C & =1\cdot (-5)+10 \\  & =-5+10 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
